title: Credential Attack Runner — Password Spraying, Kerberoasting, and Hash Cracking
goal: Add controlled credential attack capabilities: Kerberoast/AS-REP roast hash extraction, offline hash cracking via hashcat, and rate-limited password spraying — the techniques that turn enumeration results into confirmed credential access.
scope: Implement three sub-runners under workers/runners/credential_attacks/: (1) KERBEROAST runner: uses impacket GetUserSPNs.py to request Kerberos service tickets for Kerberoastable accounts (discovered by BloodHound/LDAP enum), stores TGS hashes as encrypted artifacts, produces findings per roastable account. Active tier, requires domain auth. (2) AS-REP ROAST runner: uses impacket GetNPUsers.py for AS-REP roastable accounts. Same artifact and finding handling. Active tier, requires domain account list. (3) HASHCAT offline cracker: takes encrypted hash artifacts from Responder/Kerberoast runs, runs hashcat with a configurable wordlist (default: rockyou.txt if present on Kali), crack results stored as protected secrets_refs — cracked plaintext passwords are NEVER written to findings, logs, or API payloads. A finding is produced: 'Weak password cracked for account X' with severity based on account privilege. (4) SPRAY runner (intrusive, separate approval gate): rate-limited password spraying using a configurable attempt count per window (default: 1 attempt per account per 30 minutes to avoid lockout). Requires explicit lockout policy from LDAP enum before dispatch. Cracked/sprayed credential results feed into secrets_refs for subsequent NetExec/Metasploit phases.
generation_reason: Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting are the most reliable privilege escalation paths in AD environments. NodeZero includes AD Password Audit (offline cracking) as a named feature. Without credential attack capabilities, AegisPT cannot demonstrate the real-world impact of weak service account passwords — the most common critical finding in internal assessments.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Cracked plaintext passwords are NEVER in findings, logs, or API payloads — only in encrypted secrets_refs. Spraying requires explicit lockout policy confirmation and uses a rate below the lockout threshold. Hash cracking is offline only — no cloud cracking. Kerberoast/AS-REP require domain auth context. Spray gate is separate from other intrusive gates.

success_criteria: Kerberoast runner extracts TGS hashes and stores as encrypted artifacts.
AS-REP roast runner extracts AS-REP hashes for no-preauth accounts.
Hashcat runner cracks hashes offline and stores results as secrets_refs only.
Cracked plaintext passwords never appear in findings, logs, or API payloads.
Spray runner enforces rate limiting below lockout threshold.
Spray runner requires explicit lockout policy confirmation before dispatch.
Findings reference cracked account name and privilege level without exposing password.
Separate intrusive approval gates for spray vs. Kerberoast.
Tests cover hash storage, no-plaintext enforcement, lockout gate, and rate limiting.
must_not_touch: Plaintext passwords in findings, logs, or API payloads
pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Hash extraction and cracking work with encrypted storage.
